full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Abdur Rashid. J: This Rule was obtained by the defendant Nos. 1-5 upon making an application under Section 115 of the Code of the Civil Procedure against judgment and order dated 13.03.97 passed by Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Jamalpur in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 10 of 1996 affirming those dated 02.01.96 passed by Senior Assistant Judge at Sadar, Jamalpur in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1994. 

 3. The petitioners who are defendants in the suit made an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex parte decree and also restoration of the suit to its file and number arid Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1994 was thereupon registered. 

 4. The case of the defendants in short, is that after the filing of the suit said opposite parties made an application for temporary injunction for restraining the defendants from entering into the suit land Pursuant to the notice of the said application, the petitioners appeared and filed a written objection to the prayer for temporary injunction. Learned Assistant Judge however granted the injunctions. Against the said order of injunction, petitioners preferred an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 99 of 1986 in the Court of District Judge at Jamalpur. One of the defendants Abdul Malek who used to look after the appeal died on 12.10.1990. On his death, the appeal was dismissed for default for not taking steps in the appeal. 

 5. After disposal of the appeal, the records of the case was sent clown to the lower court and the lower court on 13.06.93 received the records and fixed 07.07.93 for filing of written statement. On 05.07.93 the learned Advocate of the petitioner appears to have seen the said order but he did not inform the defendants of the arrival of the records and the date fixed for filing written statement. On 07.07.93 the suit was posted for ex parte disposal on 21.07.93. On 21.07.93 the plaintiff got their plaint amended without serving any notice on them. On 21.07.93 the suit was again fixed for ex part disposal on 29.07.93 and on that date, the son was taken up and was decreed ex parte behind the back of the petitioners. 

 7. Opposite Party No. 5(A) was added as a party in the suit. This opposite party No. 5(A) Only opposed the case of the defendants by filing a written statement oil 16.04.96. His case is that on 11.05.92 her purchased 26 decimals of land out of the stiff land from opposite party No. 1. He also purchased some more lands by other deeds. His case in brief is that after of the record from the appellate court the suit was fixed for filing the written statement on 07.07.93 and the order dated 13.06.93 was shown to the learned Advocate of the defendants. He also that the petitioners had knowledge of the dates but preferred not to appear in the trial of the suit and accordingly the was decreed ex parte. 

 10. Mr. Sultan Ahmed the learned Counsel appearing for the Rule, submits that both the courts below failed to consider the case of the petitioner that they had no knowledge about the proceedings of the suit, particularly the date fixed for pre-emptory hearing as their learned Advocate though was shown the order dated 13.06.93 on 05.07.93 but did not inform. And in the absence of any notice or information petitioners had no knowledge and both the courts below acted illegally in rejecting their application. 

 11. He cited in support of his submission, the cases reported in 44 DLR(AD) 30, 14 DLR(AD) 58, 17 DLR(SC) 487, 16 DLR (SC) 155 and 36 DLR (AD) at page 8 and 88. 

 12. The learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 5(A) submits that both the courts below found that the petitioner failed to prove their date of knowledge as was stated in their application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and there was no application filed for condonation of delay under Section 5 of the Limitation Act. The suit was decreed on 29.07.93 and application was made only on 11.05.94. In the absence of any application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act the case was correctly found barred by limitation by both courts. Such order of affirmance, does not call for any interference. 

 14. It appears that after disposal of the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 39 of 1986, the record was received by the Assistant Judge on 13.06.93. On trial date 07.07.93 was fixed for filing of written statement. That order was seen by the learned Advocate for the petitioners on 05.07.93. It is the ease of petitioners that the learned Advocate did not inform them either the date for filing written statements or the date fixed for ex party’s disposal of the suit. It also appears that on 07.07.03 the suit was for the first time fixed for ex parte disposal on 21.07.93. No on 21.07.93 the plaintiff got their plaint amended. On that day, suit was however posted for disposal ex pane on 29.07.93. It is not disputed that no copy of the application for amendment of the plaint was served on the petitioner or on their learned Advocate. When a plaint is amended the suit is generally to be taken out front the list of pre-emptory hearing in order to enable the defendants to file an additional written statement if any they want his this case within 8 days of amendment of the plaint of amendment of the plaint the snit was again posted for ex parte disposal. This hurried action of the trial court to dispose the suit without presence of the petitioners does not appear to be bonafide. 

 16. In this case pursuant to the notice of the temporary injunction the petitioners appeared and filed objection. The case or petitioners is that one of the defendants, Malek issued to look after the case as tadbirker and he died on 12.10.90. On his death no step could be taken and the appeal was dismissed for default. After arrival of the record to the trial court from the appellate Court the learned Advocate through on 05.07.93 saw the order passed on 13.06.93 but did not inform the defendants and so the defendants could not know about the progress of the suit and be present when the suit was fixed for ex parte disposal. 

 17. I find that the trial order considered the evidence of P.W 1 who slated that his brother Abdul Malek used to look after the case. But the court took the view that Abdul Malek was not examined as a witness in the case. But this finding is fully misconceived as the whole case of the petitioner is based on the fact that Abdul Malek died on 12.10.90. Appellate Court in considering the evidence of P.Ws. came to a finding that Habibur Rahman used to look after the case on behalf of the petitioners. It also disbelieved the story of the petitioner that the opposite parties went on 07.05.94 to the suit land for taking possession as the suit was for perpetual injunction and there could not be any reason for than to go to take possession of the suit land. 

 18. In the case of Keramat Ali Bhuivan V Ramizuddin Ahmed. (1991) 43 DLR (AD) 58, an application under Order 9 Rule 9 of the Code for restoration of the suit on the ground that the record of the suit was sent to this Division in connection with a first appeal sometime in 1976 and upon its receipt back no notice was given to either to the plaintiff or his learned Advocate and thus the plaintiff was prevented from appearing in court when the suit was called on for hearing on 03.01.78. The application was resisted on ground of limitation as no application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act was filed for condonation of delay. The trial court allowed the application and restored the suit to its file and number but subject to payment of Taka 300. The order was upheld in revision by this Division. Dismissing the petition for leave to appeal the Appellate Division held that when the direction of the court to inform the learned Advocate of the parties about the receiving of the record from this Division was not complied with and thus. the court had inherent jurisdiction to restore suit under due to any Section 151 of the Code. It was also observed that when an injury is caused to a party due to any mistake or default committed by a court or its officers there are high authorities laying down that in circumstances of this nature, it is not only right and the duty of the court to correct its own mistake. 

 19. In the case of M.A. Wahab and another V. Abul Kalam and another (1992) 44 DLR(AD) 13 the suit was transferred from the dearth court of Subordinate Judge at Dhaka to the second court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka in implementation of a gazette notification by the fourth court's order dated 28.01.85, which was an off-day for pleader commissioner's report. The second court received the case record on 29.01.84 and fixed 12.03.85 for report of the pleader commissioner and added "inform". This Division found that the defendant never appeared in the new court thereafter and the second court's order never shown to the defendant's Advocate. So the appeal presented by the defendant against judgment and (inter of the trial court rejecting his application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code for restoration of the suit after setting aside the ex parte decree was allowed subject to payment of Taka 3000 to the plaintiff by this Division on the ground of non-compliance of Rule 388(2) of the Civil Rides and Orders (Vol-1) in dismissing the petition for leave to appeal, the Appellate Division held that 

 20. In this case, the record of the case was received by the trial court on 13.06.93 and the court on that date fixed 07.07.93 for filing of written statement. On 05.07.93 the learned Advocate of the petitioners was shown the order dated 13.06.93. It is the positive case of the petitioners that the learned Advocate did not inform the petitioners of the receipt of the record or the date fixed for filing of written statement. It is also true that the date of knowledge r on 07.05.94 as alleged by the petitioners was not believed by the courts below. But the assertion of the petitioners that their Advocate did not inform them, it appears, did not receive any consideration by either of the courts below. Moreover, on 07.07.93 the suit was fixed for ex parte disposal on 21.07.93. But on this date, the opposite parties No. 1 to 5 as plaintiffs did not get the suit heard ex parte instead made an application for amendment of their plaint without, serving any notice upon the petitioners or their Advocate. The trial court allowed the application for amendment as prayed for and fixed 29.07.93 just after 8 days, again for ex parte disposal. The petitioners no doubt had a right to a prior notice of hearing of such application for amendment and further right to a date for filing a written statement against such amendment. It is also not disputed that the orders dated 07.07.93 and 21.07.93 were not even shown to the Advocate of the petitioners. The procedure adopted by the trial court is therefore not sanctioned by law. 

 22. In the circumstances of the case, I find that the trial court passed the orders dated 21.07.93 and 29.07.93 behind the back of the petitioners and as a result, when the suit was called on for hearing I he petitioners could not appear as they were not aware of any of the dates. The court of appeal below also missed such vital aspect of the ease. Secondly, when it the duty of a min not to pass any order behind the back of a party which would adversely affect such party and the court is also obliged to correct its own default, if any, by invoking its inherent jurisdiction its was held in the case of Keramat Ali Bhuiyan V Ramizuddin Ahmed. (1991)) 43 DLR (AD) 58, both the courts below erred in law in holding, that the delay in making Application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code could not be condoned in the absence of an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
